meta.title: Operation of Refrigerator in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To store crude drug samples, herbal extracts, standards, reagents, and biological materials at controlled low temperature (2–8°C) to prevent degradation, microbial growth, and chemical deterioration.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for short-term storage of perishable plant materials, volatile extracts, and reference standards.
procedure: Ensure the laboratory refrigerator is plugged in and operating at the set temperature (2–8°C) — verify with an internal calibrated thermometer.
Check the temperature display daily and record in the temperature log.
Before storing any material, label it clearly: material name, concentration (if applicable), date of preparation, expiry/review date, and handler's name.
Store materials in tightly sealed containers — open containers allow cross-contamination and odour transfer.
Segregate materials by category: reagents, extracts, standards, and biological specimens in designated areas or shelves.
Do not store food items in the laboratory refrigerator under any circumstances.
Do not store volatile flammable solvents (e.g., diethyl ether, petroleum ether) in a standard refrigerator — use a spark-free explosion-proof refrigerator.
Inspect stored materials weekly — discard expired, contaminated, or unlabelled items.
When adding new materials, practise FIFO (First In, First Out) — place newer items behind older ones.
Keep the refrigerator interior clean — wipe spills immediately with a damp cloth.
Defrost regularly if ice build-up exceeds 5 mm on the freezer compartment walls.
Record all temperature excursions (temperature outside 2–8°C) and take corrective action immediately.
Do not overload — maintain adequate air circulation inside.
Record door open/close times for critical storage areas in the temperature log.
precautions: Never store food alongside laboratory materials — risk of accidental ingestion and contamination.
Always label materials before placing them in the refrigerator — unlabelled items must be discarded.
Inspect the door seal regularly for wear — a damaged seal leads to temperature fluctuations.
Install a temperature alarm or data logger to alert if temperature exceeds the set range.
Do not store reactive chemicals together — segregate acids, bases, oxidizers, and flammables even at low temperature.
In case of power failure, do not open the refrigerator unnecessarily — a closed refrigerator maintains temperature for several hours.
Calibrate the internal thermometer against a reference thermometer annually.
